title: autotune: add defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Reduce unit inference cost for common production workloads by providing safe, production-ready defaults and a minimal autotune pipeline that recommends batching, KV caching, and quantization profiles per model/workload. This PR wires together three pieces: 1) default batching and KV cache config heuristics in the serving runtime; 2) a stable set of quantization profiles and automatic profile selection logic; 3) unit-economics (UEcon) tooling surfaced to the Console and CLI to evaluate expected cost/latency tradeoffs for candidate configs.

What this changes (high-level):
- Runtime: add heuristics to compute per-route batching window and target batch sizes based on historical latency distributions and SLO target. Scope: serving/runtime/batcher and serving/runtime/config.
- Caching: enable prefix KV cache default ON for chat routes with short prompt tails; introduce cache eviction threshold and hot-key detection to avoid memory blowup. Scope: serving/runtime/kv_cache.{cpp,py}.
- Quantization: provide three curated quant profiles (safe-ptq, aggressive-4bit, fp16-fallback) and runtime logic to pick a compatible profile given model architecture and accuracy budget. Scope: model-registry/quant_profiles.json and serving/runtime/quant_selector.py.
- UEcon tooling: new CLI command `redwood uecon simulate` and a Console panel showing expected cost/latency delta for candidate configs; integrates with telemetry to estimate tokens/sec and GPU utilization. Scope: redwood-console, redwood-cli, telemetry pipeline.
- Telemetry and evals: add lightweight eval harness for latency/cost regression tests and tie UEcon alerts to the eval result set.

Checklist:
- [x] Runtime batching heuristics implemented and unit-tested
- [x] KV cache defaults and safety knobs added
- [x] Quant profiles added and selector tested on subset of models
- [x] UEcon CLI and console integration implemented (beta)
- [x] End-to-end e2e test in perf-canary validating no regression >5% latency on P50/P95 for standard workloads
- [x] Docs: console help and CLI docs updated

Backward-compatibility and rollout: All changes are behind an opt-in feature flag `autotune_cost_defaults` in the serving config. The runtime will continue to use per-route explicit configs when present. We will rollout to Dedicated Beta customers first, monitor UEcon alerts for regressions, then enable for hosted-batch tier by config.

Risks and mitigations:
- Memory: KV cache defaults could increase GPU memory pressure. Mitigation: conservative default TTL and eviction policy; hot-key detection disables caching for pathological workloads.
- Accuracy: aggressive quant profiles can degrade quality. Mitigation: profiles have an associated eval harness and accuracy delta thresholds; selector prefers safe-ptq unless workload passes accuracy gates.
- Observability: new UEcon estimates are best-effort initially; Console clearly labels them as estimates with confidence bands.

Notes: This PR intentionally limits the scope of auto changes (no in-flight reconfiguration of live pods) — the initial rollout requires explicit route update to adopt recommended profile. Follow-up PRs will add safe live rollouts and canary application of quant profiles.

release_notes: Add experimental autotune defaults for batching and KV caching, curated quantization profiles, and new unit-economics simulation tooling. Feature gated behind `autotune_cost_defaults`. Console and CLI include UEcon panels/commands for cost/latency estimates. Rollout: opt-in for Dedicated Beta; monitor UEcon alerts before wider enablement.
